name: Derivation (ishtiqāq)
definition: Taking one word from another with the same root letters and a related meaning: the verb, the participles and the other derived nouns from one root.
body: From the root ḍ-r-b come ḍaraba, yaḍribu, ḍārib (striker), maḍrūb (struck) and the other derived forms. Which is the origin of derivation was a famous question between the schools: the Basrans said the maṣdar, since it names the bare event; the Kufans said the past verb, since the maṣdar follows the verb in its soundness and weakness. Ibn Jinnī added a 'greater derivation' (al-ishtiqāq al-akbar), the meaning shared by all the orders of the same three letters.

examples.text: ḍaraba, yaḍribu, ḍārib, maḍrūb: one root, one meaning, different forms.
